It is not essential to speak or understand Italian, but it is an advantage. You are affiliated with an arts organisation in Flanders that works in the field of participation, or you invite an arts organisation in Flanders to follow the process remotely, which has an interest in building relationships with socially engaged practices in the Naples region and in following up on the project after the workshop.
project_requirements: The creator/director from Flanders with a socially engaged practice is invited to work with one vulnerable group from 19 to 29 November 2026 . Examples of vulnerable groups include young people at risk, women who are victims of violence, people from migrant backgrounds, people with different abilities, or people with mental health vulnerabilities. The group of participants will be selected based on the chosen candidate and the workshop proposal, in collaboration with an Italian director. The workshop will be conducted in Italian as not all participants speak English. An Italian–English interpreter will be provided. Knowledge of English is therefore essential. The workshop will last between 4 and 6 hours per day. Short performance sessions are planned at the end of the workshop (27–30 November). The workshop will be prepared online in collaboration with the Italian director.

Participants learn the Soundpainting language, practice conducting and playing in ensemble, and finish with a presentation moment in the concert hall of Muziekcentrum De Bijloke. The academy includes guidance from leading soundpainters and members of the Safety Last Soundpainting Ensemble.

requirements_text: Leerkrachten uit het DKO of (professionele) muzikanten die de taal van soundpainting willen toepassen in de eigen les- of artistieke praktijk. Tijdens de tweede editie van deze academy moedigen we, naast muzikanten, ook dansers en performers aan om deel te nemen.
requirements_text_en: Teachers from the DKO or (professional) musicians who want to apply the language of soundpainting in their own teaching or artistic practice. During the second edition of this academy, we also encourage dancers and performers, in addition to musicians, to participate.
project_requirements: Tijdens deze driedaagse maak je kennis met of verdiep je je verder in de universele taal van soundpainting, een handige muzikale tool voor je eigen les- of artistieke praktijk. Je leert zelf soundpainten door kennis te maken met de soundpainting-tekens én je leert spelen in orkestverband. En dat doe je uiteraard niet alleen, maar onder begeleiding van toonaangevende soundpainters én met de leden van het Safety Last Soundpainting Ensemble als levende voorbeelden. Afsluiten doe je met een presentatiemoment (op een stille animatiefilm) in de concertzaal van Muziekcentrum De Bijloke.

project_requirements_en: During this three-day course, you will get acquainted with or further deepen your knowledge of the universal language of soundpainting, a handy musical tool for your own teaching or artistic practice. You will learn to soundpaint yourself by getting acquainted with the soundpainting signs, and you will learn to play in an orchestra setting. And of course you will not do that alone, but under the guidance of leading soundpainters and with the members of the Safety Last Soundpainting Ensemble as living examples. You will conclude with a presentation moment (on a silent animated film) in the concert hall of Muziekcentrum De Bijloke.

requirements_text:

We are looking for vocal performers who:
_have a classical alt / baritone/tenor vocal range
_are comfortable with live performance and embodied presence
_enjoy participatory interaction with an audience
_have affinity with music theatre, contemporary music, and/or ritual practices
_enjoy collaborative, research-driven creation processes
title_en: Auditions Conversations – New XRPerformance by Paul Boereboom & Leon Rogissart
requirements_text_en:
We are looking for classical vocal performers (classical alt, baritone or tenor, f/m/x) to join an innovative international trajectory at the intersection of live performance, music, movement, and XR technology.
We are looking for vocal performers who:
_have a classical alt / baritone/tenor vocal range
_are comfortable with live performance and embodied presence
_enjoy participatory interaction with an audience
_have affinity with music theatre, contemporary music, and/or ritual practices
_enjoy collaborative, research-driven creation processes
project_requirements:
An immersive music theatre ritual for an intimate audience of 80 participants.
In a shared space, performers and audience move together through a collective experience of music, reflection, and encounter.
The performance is participatory and interactive.
As a performer, you engage directly with the audience: you are not playing a character, but performing as yourself.
Presence, attentiveness, and openness towards the participants are central to the work.
The project explores themes of inner dialogue, presence, and collective ritual, and uses technology as a supportive dramaturgical layer rather than a dominant element.

Please send the following material to leonrogissart@gmail.com before the 23rd of February:
_A bio & a resume plus a link to a live audio or video recording of you singing (studio recordings will not be considered)
Based on submissions, a selection of candidates will be invited to an audition on the 2nd of March in Rotterdam.
Please let us know if this date is not possible in your application mail.

The workshop will be conducted in Italian because not all participants are proficient in English. An Italian-English interpreter will be provided. The duration of the workshop varies between 4 and 6 hours per day. Small performances are planned at the end of the workshop (November 27-30). The workshop starts on November 17 and ends on November 30, 2025. You agree to participate in presentations, which are currently scheduled for November 28, 29, and 30. Departure is possible from December 1, 2025.
how_to_apply: Send your motivation letter in English with a CV by Friday, September 5, at 11:59 p.m. to Julia Reist: julia.reist@kunsten.be. In the letter, indicate the type of vulnerability you have experience with and a methodology or idea for how to structure the workshop. In addition to the selection process, this will also help to make the right match between the group of participants and the Italian director. You should also indicate which languages you speak fluently. Include the name of the arts organization from Flanders that wants to follow this workshop remotely and is interested in follow-up. You or the arts organization itself should briefly explain in the motivation letter why they want to participate in this process.

title: Residency in Berlin, Bethanien
requirements_text: You must be a professional artist in the field of visual arts or design. You have an artistic practice in, for example, the visual arts, photography, design, crafts, illustration, textile art or architecture. To be considered a professional artist, you must earn a living entirely or partly from your artistic activities and regularly present your art to an audience or in an artistic context. You must be a resident in Sweden or practice most of your art here. You can be a foreign citizen and apply for our stipends and grants, but you must be a resident in Sweden or primarily practice your art here. If you are a Swedish citizen but live abroad, you must be able to demonstrate that most of your artistic activity takes place in Sweden. You must not be a student for more than 50 per cent of your time when an award decision is made. This means being enrolled in any type of studies, from undergraduate studies to doctoral studies and post-graduate education. You can be studying when you submit your application, but when a decision is made you cannot be enrolled for more than 50 per cent for a course or programme. You may not have any debts to the state or municipality that have been transferred for collection to the Swedish Enforcement Authority (Kronofogdemyndigheten), nor be declared bankrupt. You may not have tax or fee debts, or any other debts, that have been transferred to the Swedish Enforcement Authority and are being handled as a public collection matter. You must not have received de minimis aid exceeding a total of 300,000 euros during the last three-year period. Stipends and grants from the Swedish Arts Grants Committee are subject to the provisions of the European Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/2031 on state funding, also known as de minimis aid.

requirements_text:
Residence NRW⁺ richtet sich an bildende Künstler:innen und Kurator:innen mit Bezug zum Bundesland Nordrhein-Westfalen sowie an Kurator:innen aus der Schweiz.
Residence NRW⁺ richtet sich an Künstler:innen mit Bezug zum Bundeland Nordrhein-Westfalen (Herkunft, Studium oder Wohn-/Arbeitsort).
Erforderlich ist ein abgeschlossenes Studium an einer Kunstakademie/Kunsthochschule.
Der Abschluss der künstlerischen Ausbildung der Stipendiat:innen darf bei Antritt des Stipendiums nicht länger als fünf Jahre zurückliegen oder die Stipendiat:innen dürfen nicht älter als 40 Jahre sein.
Residence NRW⁺ richtet sich an Kurator:innen mit Bezug zum Bundesland Nordrhein-Westfalen bzw. der Schweiz, die profunde Kenntnisse im Bereich der zeitgenössischen Kunst besitzen und bereits eine eigene Vorstellung der kuratorischen Arbeit entwickelt haben sowie Gelegenheit hatten, erste Projekte zu realisieren.
Bewerber:innen mit Bezug zum Bundesland NRW müssen ein Universitätsstudium (Master, Diplom, Magister oder Promotion; Kunstgeschichte, Kunst, Kulturwissenschaften oder ähnliches) abgeschlossen haben; ferner gilt, dass ihr Studienabschluss bei Antritt des Stipendiums nicht länger als fünf Jahre zurückliegt oder sie nicht älter als 35 Jahre sein dürfen.
Für Bewerber:innen mit Bezug zur Schweiz gilt kein Alterslimit, jedoch darf auch hier der Abschluss der Ausbildung oder, falls keine Ausbildung vorliegt, die erste öffentliche Präsentation der kuratorischen Arbeit nicht länger als 5 Jahre zurückliegen.
requirements_text_en:
Residence NRW⁺ is aimed at visual artists and curators with a connection to the federal state of North Rhine-Westphalia as well as at curators from Switzerland.
Residence NRW⁺ is aimed at artists with a connection to the federal state of North Rhine-Westphalia (origin, studies, or place of residence/work).
A completed degree from an art academy/art university is required.
The completion of the artistic training of the fellows must not be more than five years ago at the time the fellowship begins, or the fellows must not be older than 40 years.
Residence NRW⁺ is aimed at curators with a connection to the federal state of North Rhine-Westphalia or Switzerland who possess profound knowledge in the field of contemporary art and have already developed their own conception of curatorial work and have had the opportunity to realize initial projects.
Applicants with a connection to the federal state of NRW must have completed a university degree (master's, diploma, Magister, or doctorate; art history, art, cultural studies, or similar); furthermore, their degree must not be more than five years old at the start of the fellowship or they must not be older than 35 years.
For applicants with a connection to Switzerland, there is no age limit; however, here too the completion of training or, if no training exists, the first public presentation of curatorial work must not be more than 5 years ago.
project_requirements:
Die Stipendienzeit vornehmlich am Residenzort zu verbringen und an gemeinsamen Veranstaltungen (Arbeitstreffen, Exkursionen, Eröffnungen, etc.) teilzunehmen, sind verpflichtend.
Teil des Stipendiums ist eine budgetierte Abschlussausstellung in einer Kunstinstitution in NRW.
Diese wird gemeinsam mit den anwesenden Kurator:innen entwickelt, die auch für die Umsetzung verantwortlich sind.
Im Arbeitsduo mit dem:der gleichzeitig anwesenden Kurator:in sind in der Regel zwei Projekte selbständig für wechselnde Kooperationsorte zu realisieren.

project_requirements_en:
The scholarship period is to be spent primarily at the place of residence, and participation in joint events (work meetings, excursions, openings, etc.) is mandatory.
Part of the scholarship is a budgeted final exhibition in an art institution in NRW.
This is developed together with the curators present, who are also responsible for implementation.
In the working duo with the curator present at the same time, two projects are generally to be realized independently for changing cooperation venues.

program_dates_en: Per year, Residence NRW⁺ awards four twelve-month scholarships for visual artists as well as four six-month scholarships for curators.

project_requirements: We invite 20 minute papers and pre-constituted panels with a maximum of 4 speakers that: consider the definition of video art since its inception and the major transformations the concept has gone through; review and reframe existing video histories; examine the organisational model of the video collective, and its modes of circulation and distribution; explore the international and regional video networks of which LVA was part, share new research into underacknowledged video histories and figures; address the heterogeneous and intersecting ecologies of video practice: whether conceptual documentation and modernist experiment, radical campaigning and community engagement, and the later return to representational form; address how technological changes have determined video practices, cultures and ecologies; examine how London Video Arts addressed the hegemony of broadcast TV; explore the determining role of televisual culture and production in the development of video practice: it’s forms and address. consider what contemporary collective, activist or community-based video practices, in the UK and internationally, share with or depart from LVA’s model of artist-led organising consider how video art explored the limits of its material, processes and forms; discuss the role of video to address political and social urgencies and injustices; question the legacy of analogue video technology in the digital age; address the challenges of how to archive, conserve and exhibit fragile historic video technologies; explore how museums and galleries understand video art today.

title: 5th Medialab Matadero Open Call for the Award of Three (3) Residencies within the Annual Situated Research Programme (2027)
requirements_text:
It is aimed at individuals, collectives, or cultural, artistic, scientific, technological, or research agents developing projects within the fields of situated research, contemporary creation, and transdisciplinary experimentation.
Whether the applicant is an individual, a collective, or an agent, the submitted project must reflect their own research and creative process, be coherent with their trajectory, and demonstrate the capacity to be developed within the context of an in-person residency at the Matadero Madrid Centre for Artists in Residence (hereinafter, the CRA).

title_en: 5th Medialab Matadero Open Call for the Award of Three (3) Residencies within the Annual Situated Research Programme (2027)
requirements_text_en:
It is aimed at individuals, collectives, or cultural, artistic, scientific, technological, or research agents developing projects within the fields of situated research, contemporary creation, and transdisciplinary experimentation.
Whether the applicant is an individual, a collective, or an agent, the submitted project must reflect their own research and creative process, be coherent with their trajectory, and demonstrate the capacity to be developed within the context of an in-person residency at the Matadero Madrid Centre for Artists in Residence (hereinafter, the CRA).
Submitted projects must be the work of the applicant or, in the case of collective projects, of the members of the collective.
project_requirements:
The residencies will last for seven (7) months and will take place between January and July 2027.
Submitted projects should engage with Medialab Matadero’s lines of work and operate at the margins or intersections of different disciplines, methodologies, and fields of knowledge.
Projects should adhere to the following guidelines:
 Explore potential intersections between art, design, science, technology, and society.
 Contribute to critical reflection on contemporary socio-technical, cultural, ecological, political, or urban challenges.
 Propose collaborative, experimental, situated, or unconventional research methodologies.
 Establish bonds with communities, agents, collectives, citizen initiatives, professional fields, or bodies of knowledge related to the project.
 Incorporate a public dimension through activities involving learning, dissemination, the exchange of knowledge, mediation, or the presentation of the research process.
As part of the residency, each project must develop a public programme related to its research process.
These may take the form of workshops, encounters, working groups, critical sessions, conversations, open laboratories, presentations, or other platforms for collective experimentation.
Comprising between one and six activities, this public programme will be defined and fine-tuned during the residency in dialogue with the Medialab Matadero team, in accordance with the evolution of the research, the needs of the project, and the availability of spaces and resources.
Furthermore, the selected projects must participate in a final public showcase at Medialab Matadero, scheduled to take place between June and July 2027, where they will share the processes, lessons learnt, methodologies, or findings developed during the residency.
selection_criteria:
The award of the research residencies covered by this open call will be carried out on a competitive tender basis, in accordance with the principles of public notice, open competition, transparency, objectivity, equality, and non-discrimination, as well as those relating to effectiveness in achieving the objectives of the open call and efficiency in the allocation and use of available resources.
An Evaluation Committee shall be set up to select the winning projects, examining submitted applications in accordance with the requirements, assessment criteria, and documentation established in these terms and conditions.

requirements_text_en:
Only natural persons, of legal age, with legal capacity and legal residence in Spain and who do not incur any of the prohibitions on contracting established in article 71 of the Public Sector Contracts Law, and who have their residence or main area of action in the Community of Madrid, whose documentation or trajectory proves such circumstance, may apply.

project_requirements:
La presente convocatoria, de conformidad con los principios de transparencia, igualdad y concurrencia, y en consonancia con las líneas de programación de Matadero Madrid, tiene como objeto final apoyar a un creador, colectivo o agente cultural que trabaje en el ámbito del arte y la educación dentro de un contexto de investigación, acción y producción educativa y/o artística con Matadero Madrid.

El objetivo principal de esta residencia será llevar a cabo un proceso de reflexión e investigación junto con la activación de un programa de mediación, arte y educación que se desarrolle en las instalaciones del recinto cultural y se integre conceptualmen te dentro de las líneas de investigación y acción que se desarrollan a continuación.

Los proyectos de investigación podrán abordar una u otra línea, o ambas líneas propuestas.

- Línea 1
Se incluyen en esta línea, desde la práctica de la mediación expandida y el arte y la educación, aquellas propuestas que reflexionen y reaccionen y sobre las emergencias contemporáneas propias de esta época, como son las disidencias del cuerpo y/o afectivo-sexuales; los activismos antirracistas; la emergencia climática; las transformaciones productivistas y aceleracionistas en el mundo del trabajo o la reflexión sobre la salud mental.

- Línea 2
Se incluyen en esta línea aquellos proyectos que desarrollen su investigación sobre la propia mediación y los cruces entre el arte y la educación.

Quedarán descartados aquellos proyectos destinados exclusivamente a la mediación de exposiciones o al trabajo con centros educativos. Tampoco se valorarán aquellas propuestas dirigidas a otros programas de Matadero Madrid que giren exclusivamente en torno a las artes escénicas o la creación cinematográfica.

A lo largo de la residencia, y obligatoriamente en consenso con el Departamento de educación y públicos y el Centro de residencias artísticas de Matadero Madrid, el residente podrá ir adaptando el programa público para que pueda responder tanto a los avances de su investigación como a las particularidades propias del Centro de residencias y de Matadero Madrid.

El programa público resultado de la activación de la investigación deberá comprender de 6 a 10 sesiones públicas.

Las actividades públicas incluidas en el programa podrán desarrollarse en diversos espacios de Matadero Madrid, en función de las necesidades específicas de las sesiones, así como de la disponibilidad de los mismos. El uso de los diferentes espacios deberá siempre ser aprobado previamente por el Departamento de educación y públicos y el Centro de residencias artísticas. Los espacios en los que se podrá desarrollar el programa serán principalmente los del Centro de residencias artísticas y el Taller.
selection_criteria:
Se valorarán aquellas propuestas que muestren un proyecto de investigación coherente con la trayectoria del solicitante y que constituyan un aporte a los discursos actuales de la mediación el arte y la educación.

Igualmente, se valorarán positivamente aquellas propuestas que tengan un alto componente experimental y que no encajen fácilmente en otros contextos de la educación reglada y/o del circuito artístico (galerías, museos, etc.).

Será valorable que la activación de la investigación, que implica la realización de una serie de actividades públicas (de aquí en adelante “programa público”) , se esboce demostrando su consonancia con la investigación planteada .

Será valorable que se expliciten los públicos o comunidades con los que se quiere trabajar , así como las metodologías a aplicar, especialmente aquellas que fomenten la implicación de los participantes de manera activa.
program_dates: la residencia se extenderá de octubre a junio
project_requirements_en:
This call, in accordance with the principles of transparency, equality and competition, and in line with the programming lines of Matadero Madrid, has as its final purpose to support a creator, collective or cultural agent working in the field of art and education within a context of research, action and educational and/or artistic production with Matadero Madrid.

The main objective of this residency will be to carry out a process of reflection and research together with the activation of a mediation, art and education program that takes place in the facilities of the cultural venue and is conceptually integrated within the lines of research and action developed below.

The research projects may address one or the other line, or both proposed lines.

• Line 1
Included in this line, from the practice of expanded mediation and art and education, are those proposals that reflect on and react to the contemporary emergencies of this time, such as bodily and/or affective-sexual dissidences; anti-racist activisms; the climate emergency; the productivist and accelerationist transformations in the world of work; or reflection on mental health.

• Line 2
Included in this line are those projects that develop their research on mediation itself and the intersections between art and education.

Projects intended exclusively for the mediation of exhibitions or for work with educational centers will be excluded. Nor will proposals aimed at other Matadero Madrid programs that revolve exclusively around performing arts or film creation be considered.

Throughout the residency, and obligatorily in consensus with the Education and Publics Department and the Artistic Residencies Center of Matadero Madrid, the resident may adapt the public program so that it can respond both to the progress of their research and to the particularities of the Residencies Center and Matadero Madrid.

The public program resulting from the activation of the research must comprise 6 to 10 public sessions.

The public activities included in the program may take place in various spaces of Matadero Madrid, depending on the specific needs of the sessions, as well as their availability. The use of the different spaces must always be previously approved by the Education and Publics Department and the Artistic Residencies Center. The spaces in which the program may be developed will mainly be those of the Artistic Residencies Center and the Workshop.
selection_criteria_en:
Those proposals that show a research project coherent with the applicant's trajectory and that constitute a contribution to current discourses on mediation, art and education will be valued.

Likewise, those proposals that have a high experimental component and that do not easily fit into other contexts of formal education and/or the artistic circuit (galleries, museums, etc.) will be positively valued.

It will be valued that the activation of the research, which implies the realization of a series of public activities (hereinafter “public program”), is outlined demonstrating its consonance with the proposed research.

It will be valued that the publics or communities with which one wants to work are made explicit, as well as the methodologies to be applied, especially those that foster the active involvement of participants.

title: Javni poziv za financiranje oglednih prijevoda djela hrvatskih autora na strane jezike u 2026. godini
requirements_text: Na Javni se poziv mogu prijaviti fizičke i pravne osobe registrirane za izdavačku djelatnost, zastupanje/posredovanje i/ili prodaju autorskih prava koji su do sada zaključili najmanje 5 ugovora za prodaju izdavačkih prava hrvatskih autora. Prijavitelji moraju biti nositelji autorskih prava za djela koja prijavljuju na ovaj Javni poziv ili moraju posjedovati pisanu izjavu nositelja autorskih prava da su suglasni s izradom i korištenjem oglednog prijevoda u skladu s ciljevima Javnog poziva. Ako posjeduju pisanu suglasnost najmanje pet autora za financiranje oglednih prijevoda mogu se prijaviti udruge i umjetničke organizacije, odnosno autorske strukovne udruge zainteresirane za promidžbu hrvatske književnosti u inozemstvu.
title_en: Public Call for Funding Sample Translations of Works by Croatian Authors into Foreign Languages in 2026
requirements_text_en: Natural and legal persons registered for publishing activities, representation/intermediation and/or the sale of copyright who have so far concluded at least 5 contracts for the sale of publishing rights of Croatian authors may apply to the Public Call. Applicants must be holders of copyright for the works they apply with under this Public Call or must possess a written statement from the copyright holder that they agree to the preparation and use of a sample translation in accordance with the objectives of the Public Call. If they possess written consent from at least five authors for funding sample translations, associations and artistic organizations, i.e. authors’ professional associations interested in the promotion of Croatian literature abroad, may apply.
project_requirements: Ogledni prijevod koji se prijavljuje na Javni poziv mora biti prvi prijevod izvornog književnog ili neknjiževnog djela napisanog na hrvatskom jeziku na određeni strani jezik. Poželjni su ogledni prijevodi na engleski jezik, ali su prihvatljivi i drugi jezici s izrazitim promidžbenim potencijalom. Jedan prijavitelj može tražiti potporu za najmanje 10, a najviše 20 oglednih prijevoda, i to najviše 3 prijevoda pojedinog djela istoga autora. Svaka prijave treba sadržavati prijedloge za prevođenje oglednih prijevoda djela najmanje 3 različita hrvatska autora. Ogledni prijevod mora iznositi najmanje 15, a najviše 30 autorskih kartica proznog teksta, odnosno najmanje 5, a najviše 10 pjesama (od 75 do 150 stihova). S korisnikom sredstava sklopit će se ugovor kojim će se regulirati obaveze korisnika i Ministarstva kulture i medija. Korisnik sredstava za financiranje oglednih prijevoda putem ovog Javnog poziva dužan je dopustiti objavu financiranih oglednih prijevoda na mrežnim stranicama https://www.croatian-literature.hr/ bez ikakve naknade za Ministarstvo kulture i medija te omogućiti Ministarstvu korištenje sufinanciranih oglednih prijevoda u promidžbene svrhe bez ikakve naknade. Korisnik je dužan najkasnije do 1. prosinca tekuće godine dostaviti potpuno financijsko izvješće s dokazima o provedenim transakcijama, sufinancirane ogledne prijevode u tiskanom i elektroničkom obliku, kao i 10 primjeraka promidžbene knjižice ako su odobrena sredstva za tisak.

project_requirements_en: The sample translation submitted to the Public Call must be the first translation of the original literary or non-literary work written in the Croatian language into a specific foreign language. Sample translations into English are preferred, but other languages with strong promotional potential are also acceptable. One applicant may request support for at least 10 and at most 20 sample translations, with no more than 3 translations of a single work by the same author. Each application must contain proposals for translating sample translations of works by at least 3 different Croatian authors. The sample translation must comprise at least 15 and at most 30 author’s sheets of prose text, or at least 5 and at most 10 poems (from 75 to 150 verses). An agreement will be concluded with the beneficiary of the funds, regulating the obligations of the beneficiary and the Ministry of Culture and Media. The beneficiary of the funds for financing sample translations through this Public Call is obliged to allow the publication of the financed sample translations on the website https://www.croatian-literature.hr/ without any compensation for the Ministry of Culture and Media and to enable the Ministry to use the co-financed sample translations for promotional purposes without any compensation. The beneficiary is obliged, no later than 1 December of the current year, to submit a complete financial report with evidence of the executed transactions, the co-financed sample translations in printed and electronic form, as well as 10 copies of the promotional booklet if funds for printing have been approved.

title: Javni poziv za iskaz interesa za sudjelovanje u pilot-projektu Kulturna iskaznica
requirements_text:
Pružatelj usluga pristupa kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima pravna je ili fizička osoba koja obavlja registriranu djelatnost upisana u Upisnik pružatelja usluga pristupa kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima namijenjenih korisnicima Kulturne iskaznice koja prihvaća Kulturnu iskaznicu kao sredstvo plaćanja.
Pružatelji usluga pristupa kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima koji su se prijavili na ovaj Poziv i kojima je Ministarstvo kulture i medija Republike Hrvatske dalo suglasnost za sudjelovanje u programu sukladno točki III. Javnog poziva.
Na Javni poziv za iskaz interesa mogu se prijaviti isključivo sadržaji koji podliježu naplati. Prijave onih kulturnih sadržaja koji se krajnjim korisnicima nude bez naknade (besplatni sadržaji) neće se razmatrati.
title_en: Public call for expressions of interest for participation in the pilot project Cultural Card
requirements_text_en:
A provider of access to cultural and media content is a legal or natural person who performs a registered activity entered in the Register of providers of access to cultural and media content intended for users of the Cultural Card and who accepts the Cultural Card as a means of payment.
Providers of access to cultural and media content who applied to this Call and to whom the Ministry of Culture and Media of the Republic of Croatia gave consent to participate in the program in accordance with point III of the Public Call.
Only content subject to payment may apply to the Public Call for expressions of interest. Applications for cultural content offered to end users without charge (free content) will not be considered.
project_requirements:
Kulturna iskaznica može se koristiti isključivo na prodajnim mjestima koja nude kulturne sadržaje (muzeji, kinodvorane, knjižare, kazališta, koncertne dvorane, pučka otvorena učilišta, kulturni centri…), odnosno kod pružatelja usluga pristupa kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima koji sudjeluju u programu na temelju prijave na ovaj Poziv i uz suglasnost Ministarstva kulture i medija Republike Hrvatske te kod drugih subjekata koji u ime pružatelja usluga pristupa kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima nude kulturne sadržaje (dalje u tekstu: Posrednici).
Sredstva dodijeljena putem Kulturne iskaznice mogu se koristiti isključivo kod pružatelja usluga pristupa kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima i Posrednika evidentiranih u Sustavu „Kooltura - Kulturna iskaznica“ i za odabrane proizvode.
U svrhu zaštite privatnosti, prilikom učitavanja fotografija u web aplikaciju sustava Kulturne iskaznice, pružatelji sadržaja ovlašteni su objavljivati isključivo fotografije prostora, kazališnih predstava, izložbi i ostalih kulturnih sadržaja. Napominjemo kako je nužno izbjegavati objavu fotografija na kojima su vidljiva lica posjetitelja, bez obzira na to radi li se o maloljetnim ili punoljetnim osobama.
how_to_apply:
Prijave se podnose putem sustava „Kooltura - Kulturna iskaznica“.
Sustav pružateljima usluga pristupa kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima omogućuje podnošenje prijave na ovaj Poziv.
program_dates: Mladi koji od 1. siječnja do 31. prosinca 2026. godine navrše 18 godina ostvaruju pravo na izdavanje kulturne iskaznice, odnosno pristup kulturnim i medijskim sadržajima u doznačenom iznosu, koju mogu koristiti do navršenih 19 godina.
project_requirements_en:
The Cultural Card may be used exclusively at points of sale that offer cultural content (museums, cinemas, bookstores, theatres, concert halls, public open universities, cultural centres…), that is, with providers of access to cultural and media content participating in the programme on the basis of an application to this Call and with the consent of the Ministry of Culture and Media of the Republic of Croatia, as well as with other entities that, on behalf of providers of access to cultural and media content, offer cultural content (hereinafter: Intermediaries).
Funds allocated through the Cultural Card may be used exclusively with providers of access to cultural and media content and Intermediaries recorded in the “Kooltura - Cultural Card” System and for selected products.
For the purpose of privacy protection, when uploading photographs to the web application of the Cultural Card system, content providers are authorised to publish only photographs of spaces, theatre performances, exhibitions and other cultural content. Please note that it is necessary to avoid publishing photographs in which the faces of visitors are visible, regardless of whether they are minors or adults.
how_to_apply_en:
Applications are submitted via the “Kooltura - Cultural Card” system.
The system enables providers of access to cultural and media content to submit an application to this Call.
program_dates_en: Young people who turn 18 between 1 January and 31 December 2026 are entitled to the issuance of a cultural card, that is, access to cultural and media content in the allocated amount, which they may use until they turn 19.

project_requirements: Otkupom knjiga obuhvaćat će se knjige hrvatskih izdavača na hrvatskome jeziku i to: vrijedna djela suvremene domaće književnosti, prijevodi suvremene svjetske književnosti, djela od temeljne vrijednosti za nacionalnu kulturu i umjetnost, djela domaće i prijevodne (književne, znanstvene i stručne) esejistike i publicistike vrijedne knjige i slikovnice za djecu i mlade. Za otkup narodnim knjižnicama propisivat će se knjige na hrvatskom jeziku objavljene od listopada 2025. i tijekom 2026. godine koje u trenutku prijave na Javni poziv nisu starije od 6 mjeseci, samo onih nakladnika koji se pridržavaju Sporazuma o jedinstvenoj cijeni knjige (.pdf) i koji su dostavili obvezne primjerke prijavljenog izdanja Nacionalnoj i sveučilišnoj knjižnici. project_requirements_en: The purchase of books will include books by Croatian publishers in the Croatian language, namely: valuable works of contemporary domestic literature, translations of contemporary world literature, works of fundamental value for national culture and art, works of domestic and translated (literary, scientific and professional) essay writing and journalism, valuable books and picture books for children and young people. title: Javni poziv za predlaganje članova kulturnih vijeća pri Ministarstvu kulture i medija
requirements_text:
Pozivaju se ustanove u kulturi, umjetničke organizacije i udruge te druge pravne i fizičke osobe koje obavljaju djelatnost u području kulture i umjetnosti da podnesu pisane i obrazložene prijedloge kandidata za članove kulturnih vijeća pri Ministarstvu kulture i medija (u daljnjem tekstu: Vijeća) za svako pojedino područje djelovanja Vijeća, kako slijedi:
‒ za knjigu i nakladništvo
‒ za dramsku i plesnu umjetnost
‒ za glazbenu i glazbeno-scensku umjetnost
‒ za vizualne umjetnosti
‒ za međunarodnu kulturnu suradnju
‒ za interdisciplinarne i nove umjetničke i kulturne prakse.
Za članove Vijeća imenuju se umjetnici, stručnjaci i kulturni djelatnici istaknuti u područjima umjetnosti i kulture.
title_en: Public Call for Proposals for Members of the Cultural Councils at the Ministry of Culture and Media
requirements_text_en:
Cultural institutions, artistic organizations and associations, as well as other legal and natural persons engaged in activities in the field of culture and the arts, are invited to submit written and reasoned proposals of candidates for members of the cultural councils at the Ministry of Culture and Media (hereinafter: the Councils) for each individual field of the Councils’ activities, as follows:
‒ for books and publishing
‒ for dramatic and dance art
‒ for musical and musical-stage art
‒ for visual arts
‒ for international cultural cooperation
‒ for interdisciplinary and new artistic and cultural practices.
Artists, experts and cultural workers distinguished in the fields of art and culture are appointed as members of the Councils.

title: Žádosti o dotace SFK na rok 2026
requirements_text:
Jeden žadatel může podat maximálně tři žádosti ročně.
Ve výzvě se nově objevuje kategorie „ celoroční činnost “. Ta je určena pro subjekty, jejichž projekt spočívá v realizaci celoroční kontinuální činnosti (tj. zejména celoroční činnost institucí/ souborů nebo kontinuální vydávání periodik, obsahující dílčí výstupy celoročně probíhajícího projektu.
Žádosti o podporu celoroční činnosti by měly předkládat zejména ty subjekty , jež mají opravdu dlouhodobý a konkrétní plán své činnosti a realizují svůj projekt po celý kalendářní rok.
Jinými slovy subjekty, jež mají definitivně stanovený celoroční vydavatelský plán (časopisy, nakladatelství) anebo uzavřený plán výstav, koncertů, vzniku nových představení včetně termínů a podmínek jejich uvedení.

requirements_text_en:
One applicant may submit a maximum of three applications per year.
A new category, “year-round activity,” has newly appeared in the call. It is intended for entities whose project consists of carrying out year-round continuous activity (i.e. especially year-round activity of institutions/ensembles or continuous publication of periodicals, containing partial outputs of a project running throughout the year.
Applications for support of year-round activity should be submitted especially by those entities that truly have a long-term and specific plan for their activity and implement their project throughout the entire calendar year.
In other words, entities that have a definitively established year-round publishing plan (magazines, publishers) or a closed plan of exhibitions, concerts, and the creation of new performances, including the dates and conditions of their presentation.
The category of “year-round activity” is not intended for submitting applications for support of year-round operation of ensembles or institutions, or for reprising already existing works.

title: Art Commission
requirements_text: Anyone can apply, except for individual artists, art education institutions, post-graduate institutions and predominantly sales-oriented commercial art institutions. The applicant must be established in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. The commissioned artist must have worked as a professional visual artist for at least 1 year: If the artist has completed a Bachelor’s degree programme (HBO) with a visual arts curriculum, the date on the diploma will be considered the start of their professional practice. If the artist has not completed a Bachelor’s degree programme (HBO) with a visual arts curriculum, the date on which they first presented work in professional art circles will be considered the start of their professional practice. The commissioned artist must be artistically active in the visual arts and in that capacity be embedded in the professional visual arts practice in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. For artists with a non-Dutch nationality, proof of registration in the Netherlands is also required.

A realistic fee for the artist is mandatory, and must be included in the budget, in addition to the production costs. If the project concerns a permanent work of art, it may not be moved or traded without permission of the Mondriaan Fund. In that case, realistic compensation must also be paid to the artist.

description: A continuous grant for galleries and publishers taking part in international art fairs or art book fairs. It supports presentations of living visual artists or publications about contemporary visual arts from the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. The grant helps cover stand rental for participation outside the Netherlands.
funding:
For galleries: Stand rental to participate in an art fair with visual art from the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom.
How much
The maximum grant depends on the percentage of work in the presentation by visual artists from the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, and the cost of the (basic) stand rental.
Percentage of presented works by visual artists from the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom:
Less than 40%: grant is not available.
40% to 80%: 50% of the basic stand rental up to the maximum grant.
More than 80%: 80% of the basic stand rental up to the maximum grant.
Stand rental: Less than € 20,000: maximum grant is € 4,750.
€ 20.000 to 30,000: maximum granti is € 6,750.
More than € 30,000: maximum grant is € 9,000.

requirements_text:
For Dutch and non-Dutch galleries that subscribe to the Gallery Fair Practice Code, and publishers of art books.
Dutch and non-Dutch galleries participating in an art fair outside of the Netherlands, and that subscribe to the Gallery Fair Practice Code, can apply for a contribution to support presentations of work by living visual artists from the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom.
The artists from the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom must be artistically and substantively active within the visual arts field, and in this capacity, part of the professional art practice in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom.

Art galleries can apply for a grant to cover stand rental, but not to cover furnishing costs, VAT/BTW sales tax or other costs.

project_requirements: To implement a specific plan, tied to a clear working period. It can also involve collaboration. The grant is to help cover project costs, such as the execution of a concrete plan for new work, a collaboration, a period of travel or a working period. It may also entail research, mentoring or a stay at a residency in the Netherlands or abroad. The duration of the contribution must be justified by a global timeline, included in your plan. Applicants are obliged to contribute at least 10% of the total sum being requested from the Mondriaan Fund. This can be in the form of a personal investment, contributions from third parties, an interest-free loan from Fonds Kwadraat or a contribution raised through crowdfunding. This means that the contribution from the Mondriaan Fund will be for a maximum of 90% of the costs that are eligible for the grant. If the application involves another party, such as an art venue, museum, gallery, company or client, the financial contribution from this party must be in acceptable proportion to the contribution requested from the Mondriaan Fund. Cultural institutions are expected to subscribe to the Fair Practice Code. Compliance with the Fair Practice Code automatically means that the institution implements the Guideline for Artists’ Fees. What is eligible: The cost of materials specifically related to the project. Rental of equipment and materials. If equipment is purchased that is strictly necessary for the project, the depreciation costs can be included in the budget. Travel expenses for a return flight, train journey or mileage allowance to and from the main location as stated in the application. Local travel expenses are part of the contribution covering time investment. Hiring third parties (including travel and accommodation expenses, if applicable). Residency expenses: Please note that the contribution covering time investment is halved if a residency fee is included in the budget, or if it becomes apparent that the residency covers the following expenses: accommodation and meals. In the case of an artist’s book, the contribution may only be used for a special publication that can be considered an autonomous work of art in its own right and is produced in an edition of no more than 3 copies. The Artist Project grant may not be used for other publications, but the Publication grant is available for such projects. What is not eligible: Regular expenses, such as ongoing housing costs and child care are not eligible for a grant. The grant is not intended for work for an organisation, for regular work activities, exhibition costs or other costs of presenting work. The grant cannot be used to put previously produced work back into production, to frame work or transfer it to a different medium. Costs associated with a stay abroad and that are covered by the contribution for time investment include accommodation, meals and local travel expenses. An application can be made for these costs for third parties involved with the project. The Artist Project grant may not be used for a working period in a guest studio in the Netherlands or abroad if this studio is offered in the Mondriaan Fund’s Residency The Artist Project grant may not be used for activities or a project at institutions/art venues receiving long-term financial support from one of the Rijkscultuurfondsen (public cultural funds) or the Basic Cultural Infrastructure (BIS), unless it concerns non-standard programming.
how_to_apply: Applications can be submitted at any time of the year, using our online application system. You will require an account before you can submit an application. If you do not already have an account, please apply for one on this website. Keep in mind that a 3-month period is required for processing the applications.

title: Curator Researcher
requirements_text: Independent curators, critics, theorists and art observers who have been professionally active in the visual arts or cultural heritage field for at least 2 years. You are artistically and substantively active within the visual arts and/or cultural heritage field, and in this capacity, part of the professional art and/or cultural heritage practice in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. The Curator Researcher grant cannot be used to finance study. It is also not permitted to use the grant while enrolled to study at educational institutions for e.g. Bachelor’s, Master’s or postdoctoral programmes. This also applies to participation in programmes at postgraduate institutions. The contribution is not intended for work on behalf of an organisation or for regular work. The contribution may not be used for a working period in a guest studio in the Netherlands or abroad if this studio is offered in the Mondriaan Fund’s Residency programme. The contribution may not be used for production, such as of a publication or exhibition, for (cultural-) historical research or organisational archival research. At the time of submitting the application, you must not be receiving any other financial contribution from the Mondriaan Fund which, in the opinion of the board of the Mondriaan Fund, would cover the same costs. A curator or art observer can be awarded a contribution to cover time investment for no more than 24 months within a period of 48 months. A curator or art observer who is rejected on the grounds of the criterion ‘quality and development of working practice’ is not permitted to submit a new application within a period of 12 months after the initial application.

title: Protected Cultural Heritage
requirements_text:
The Protected Cultural Heritage grant is intended for owners and managers of objects and collections that are registered as protected in the Register , within the meaning of the Heritage Act (Erfgoedwet).
Applications must be submitted by the owners or managers of a protected object or protected collection.
The application must concern an object or collection listed with the Register within the meaning of the Cultural Heritage Act.
The applicant is expected to pay for a significant share of the expenses itself.
If the application concerns an object which must be renovated or restored, it is expected that this object will be accessible to the public at certain regularly scheduled times of the week, without any need for an appointment.
If the application concerns moveable industrial heritage, the renovation or restoration efforts must be designed to restore the object to an operational condition.
The applicant must be able to prove that the preservation of the object is guaranteed in the long term due to proper constructional provisions, climate control and security measures.

requirements_text:
Visual artists from the Netherlands and the Caribbean part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
Applications may only be submitted by artists who have been active as a professional visual artist for at least 1 year:
If you have completed a Bachelor’s degree programme (HBO) with a visual arts curriculum, the date on your diploma will be considered the start of your professional practice.
If there is an interim period between your graduation from the Bachelor’s programme with a visual arts curriculum and the start of your Master’s programme, this period will count as part of your professional practice.
If you have not completed a Bachelor’s degree programme (HBO) with a visual arts curriculum, the date on which you first presented work in professional art circles will be considered the start of your professional practice.
In order to be eligible for support, you must be artistically active within the visual arts field, and in this capacity, part of the professional visual arts practice in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom.
You cannot apply for or use a contribution while enrolled to study at educational institutions for e.g. Bachelor’s, Master’s or postdoctoral programmes. This also applies to participation in programmes at postgraduate institutions, and to PhD programmes. The exception is part-time programmes (not Bachelor’s programmes) of less than 20 hours a week.
Artisans live in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, and have been working as a professional artisan for at least one year.

project_requirements: The Artist with Child Voucher can only be applied for in the case of one-off, temporary and additional care/travel and/or accommodation costs for a child who is not yet of compulsory school age and for whom the applicant is responsible. These costs arise as a result of a multi-day activity of a temporary nature, such as a residency period or construction phase of an exhibition. This must be evident from a registration, commitment or invitation from the institution where the multi-day activity takes place and financial proof such as an agreement and invoice from the childcare agency or the babysitter. NB: if you hire non-professional childcare, such as a family member or someone from your own personal circle, the Mondriaan Fund charges an hourly rate of €10.25 excluding VAT with a maximum of 8 hours per day. The Artist with Child Voucher cannot be applied for during the term of another financial grant from the Mondriaan Fund if the fund board is of the opinion that the contribution covers the same costs. The Artist with Child Voucher cannot be requested for (extra) hours at the Daycare with which a permanent agreement has already been made. The Artist with Child Voucher can be awarded a maximum of 3 times per 12 months, provided that the multi-day activities for which the applications have been requested are separate. It is not possible to request multiple vouchers for costs incurred as a result of the same activity. An Artist with Child Voucher cannot be requested again for additional extra costs that arise as a result of a multi-day activity for which a Voucher has been requested.

project_requirements_en: The Artist with Child Voucher can only be applied for in the case of one-off, temporary and additional care/travel and/or accommodation costs for a child who is not yet of compulsory school age and for whom the applicant is responsible. These costs arise as a result of a multi-day activity of a temporary nature, such as a residency period or construction phase of an exhibition. This must be evident from a registration, commitment or invitation from the institution where the multi-day activity takes place and financial proof such as an agreement and invoice from the childcare agency or the babysitter. NB: if you hire non-professional childcare, such as a family member or someone from your own personal circle, the Mondriaan Fund charges an hourly rate of €10.25 excluding VAT with a maximum of 8 hours per day. The Artist with Child Voucher cannot be applied for during the term of another financial grant from the Mondriaan Fund if the fund board is of the opinion that the contribution covers the same costs. The Artist with Child Voucher cannot be requested for (extra) hours at the Daycare with which a permanent agreement has already been made. The Artist with Child Voucher can be awarded a maximum of 3 times per 12 months, provided that the multi-day activities for which the applications have been requested are separate. It is not possible to request multiple vouchers for costs incurred as a result of the same activity. An Artist with Child Voucher cannot be requested again for additional extra costs that arise as a result of a multi-day activity for which a Voucher has been requested.

title: Voucher Development
requirements_text:
Visual artists from the Netherlands and the Caribbean part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
Applications may only be submitted by artists who have been active as a professional visual artist for at least 1 year:
In order to be eligible for support, you must be artistically active within the visual arts field, and in this capacity, part of the professional visual arts practice in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom.
You cannot apply for or use a contribution while enrolled to study at educational institutions for e.g. Bachelor’s, Master’s or postdoctoral programmes. This also applies to participation in programmes at postgraduate institutions, and to PhD programmes. The exception is part-time programmes (not Bachelor’s programmes) of less than 20 hours a week.
The Development Voucher cannot be awarded to an artist who received an Artist Start grant less than 1 year prior, or an Artist Basic grant less than 4 years prior.

Or engaging the knowledge or expertise of third parties, whether it be of a substantive or technical nature, or a combination of the two.
Applications for the Development Voucher can only be submitted for a plan to develop and/or broaden your professional practice.
This should be supported by your substantive motivation and a quotation, registration, commitment from the person, institution, course or workshop in question.
If you plan to purchase specific equipment, you must substantiate how this will contribute to the development or broadening of your professional practice.
Applications for the Development Voucher made during the term of any other financial support from theMondriaan Fund will not be accepted in the case that the board is of the opinion that the contribution covers the same expenses.

title: Voucher International
requirements_text:
Visual artists, independent curators, art critics and art observers based in the Netherlands and the Caribbean part of the Kingdom.
For artists: You must have been working as a professional visual artist for at least 1 year: If you have completed a Bachelor’s degree programme (HBO) with a visual arts curriculum, the date on your diploma will be considered the start of your professional practice. If there is an interim period between your graduation from the Bachelor’s programme with a visual arts curriculum and the start of your Master’s programme, this period will be considered as part of your professional practice. If you have not completed a Bachelor’s degree programme (HBO) with a visual arts curriculum, the date on which you first presented work in professional art circles will be considered the start of your professional practice. In order to be eligible for a contribution, you must be artistically and substantively active within the visual arts field, and in this capacity, part of the professional art practice in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. You may not apply for the Voucher International contribution while studying at educational institutions for e.g. Bachelor’s, Master’s or postdoctoral programmes. This also applies to participation in programmes at postgraduate institutions. In the case that a visual artist studies part-time (not a Bachelor’s degree programme) for less than 20 hours a week, a grant may be awarded if: the applicant has been professionally active as an artist for at least 3 years, or has attended a Bachelor’s degree programme (HBO) at a visual arts educational institution for at least 3 years and has subsequently been professionally active as an artist for at least 1 year.
For curators, critics and art observers: You have been working as a professional curator, art critic or art observer in the field of visual art for at least 2 years, and can support this with publications, exhibitions, research and/or projects. You may not apply for the Voucher International contribution while studying at educational institutions for e.g. Bachelor’s, Master’s or postdoctoral programmes. This also applies to participation in programmes at postgraduate institutions. In order to be eligible for a contribution, you must be artistically and substantively active within the visual arts field, and in this capacity, part of the professional art practice in the Netherlands and/or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. For curators and art observers, the activity associated with the application must be part of their independent practice.

The artist, curator or art observer has received an invitation from a contemporary visual art institution, venue, festival or symposium outside of the Netherlands with demonstrable and internationally recognised programming in the field of contemporary visual art.

You can come from the arts and culture sector or from other fields and sectors, as long as arts and/or culture play a central role in the initiative. Applicants and partners can be based both within and outside the Nordic Region. What matters is that the initiative as a whole has a clear and meaningful connection to the Nordic Region.

project_requirements: To be eligible for funding through ENTER, your initiative must have a Nordic anchoring and be built on collaboration across borders. Arts and culture must be a significant part of the initiative, but we also encourage collaborations with other sectors, practices and areas of society. ENTER does not support initiatives whose primary purpose is: education or study visits participation in conferences, festivals, events or similar activities tours or travelling exhibitions productions or publications organisational running costs or core funding construction projects or the purchase of technical equipment for day-to-day operations You can only apply for activities that take place after you have received the funding decision from the Nordic Culture Fund. Your initiative must be completed and reported on no later than one year after the stated start date. As a general rule, the project periods for ENTER cannot be extended.
how_to_apply: Applications must be submitted electronically through the Nordic Culture Fund’s application portal.
selection_criteria: The Nordic Culture Fund will base its funding decisions on an overall assessment of each individual initiative. Among other things, we will consider the initiative’s potential to generate new developments or momentum, its potential impact and the significance it may have in a Nordic context. We will value ambition and curiosity very high, as well as recognise learning as a valuable outcome in its own right. All eligible applications are assessed against three criteria: Ambition and collaboration Does your initiative demonstrate a clear ambition to explore, test or develop something that you can show is important? And how will you work together to achieve it? Learning and transformative potential Does the initiative have the potential to generate new knowledge, relationships, ways of working or foundations for further and future development? Significance in a Nordic context Will the initiative create meaningful connections, perspectives or opportunities that have the potential to contribute positively in a Nordic context?

project_requirements: You can apply for funding from Volt for projects relating to the cultural and artistic creativity of children and young people. In this context, Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Åland are considered as Nordic countries. Projects can include: the production of works or other initiatives featuring creative content the introduction of an exchange or long-term co-operation for the target group activities that create dialogue, discussion, or debate around the Nordic languages, art, and culture. Funding is not available for: operating costs sports activities study trips or teaching scholarships scout activities political activities commercial projects or commercial activities intended to generate a financial profit projects completed or commenced before a decision is made regarding funding and subsequently sent to the applicant. The earliest start date for activities funded by the programme is six weeks after the application deadline. Projects may run during the year in which the application is submitted and the following two calendar years (i.e. the application year plus two additional years).

The applicant must not be in arrears to any public entity. The applicant’s debt position toward public entities must be documented.

Writers can submit original full-length plays in English for consideration for programming and development, including Writers’ Groups and Open Submissions Festivals. The theatre reads and responds to submissions and may offer active feedback and support to writers it is most excited about.
description_en: The Royal Court Theatre is accepting open script submissions for new plays. Writers can submit original full-length plays in English for consideration for programming and development, including Writers’ Groups and Open Submissions Festivals. The theatre reads and responds to submissions and may offer active feedback and support to writers it is most excited about.
title: Submit Your Play
requirements_text: Anyone writing in English, from the UK and around the world, can send us a play. We do not accept screenplays, novels, poetry or radio plays. We only read original, full-length plays (we suggest this would be from around 50 pages or 25-30 pages for a monologue). We are unable to accept more than one submission from a writer at a time, nor consider unsolicited resubmissions or new drafts of plays we have previously read. We do accept scripts for original musicals but cannot accept scores or soundtracks as part of first submission. We very rarely programme adaptations and therefore do not accept adaptations of novels, films or pre-existing narrative works through our open submissions – we are looking for original plays. Similarly, we are unlikely to programme plays based on histories or biographies, unless handled in a compellingly contemporary way.

project_requirements:
Résidence « ateliers familles » sur la biodiversité des jardins du Val Rahmeh (Menton) et de la Villa Arson (Nice)
du 18 octobre au 2 novembre 2025
• Lieu d’intervention : Jardin botanique du Val Rahmeh et Villa Arson
• Public concerné : familles (enfants à partir de 4 ans)
• Dates : pendant les vacances scolaires d’automne du 18 octobre au 2 novembre 2025 :
Mercredis 22 et 29 octobre / vendredis 24 et 31 octobre au Val Rahmeh et dimanche 2 novembre pour la conférence-rencontre avec Les amis du Val Rahmeh
Jeudis 23 et 30 octobre / samedis 25 octobre et 1er novembre à la Villa Arson
Nombre d’heures d’interventions : 
6h de formation correspondant à 3h/site (pour la découverte des jardins)
8h de conception correspondant à 4h/atelier (avec accompagnement par le service des publics pour l’accueil des publics familles)
12h d’animation correspondant à 4 ateliers d’1h30 à la Villa Arson et 4 ateliers d’1h30 au Val Rahmeh + une conférence-rencontre d’1h30
L’atelier proposé devra entrer en résonnance avec la devise du Muséum national d’Histoire naturelle : « Émerveiller pour instruire et pour agir ».
L’atelier proposé devra offrir une expérience sensible des jardins de la Villa Arson avec une attention portée aux enjeux de la biodiversité en cohérence avec la pratique de l’artiste.
how_to_apply:
Éléments du dossier : note d’intention de 2500 caractères (espaces compris) maximum + un portfolio de réalisations personnelles.
À envoyer par mail au plus tard le dimanche 29 juin à l’adresse suivante : servicedespublics@villa-arson.org

• Target audience: families (children from 4 years old)

project_requirements: Arenaen eller infrastrukturen du søker tilskudd til, må brukes til profesjonell kunst- og kulturaktivitet, eller til samarbeid mellom profesjonelt og frivillig kunst- og kulturliv. Prosjektet du søker tilskudd til, må komme kunst- og kulturfeltene og/eller et allment publikum til gode. Kulturrådet forutsetter at prosjektet gjennomføres i tråd med offentlig lovverk. how_to_apply: Søknaden må leveres gjennom Kulturrådets søknadsportal. Du kan velge mellom to ulike skjematyper: Investeringsstøtte kulturbygg: for søknader om om tilskudd til å bygge om, oppgradere eller tilpasse eksisterende lokaler og infrastruktur, til nybygg og til å kjøpe inn teknisk utstyr til visning eller produksjon. Enkeltprosjekter: for søknader om tilskudd til forprosjekter eller utprøvingsprosjekter. Eksempler på dette er behovsanalyser, mulighetsstudier, skisseprosjekter eller prosjektering av bygg eller tiltak, avklaring av reguleringsbestemmelser, arkitektkonkurranser eller andre tiltak som faller innenfor ordningens formål. Nedenfor har vi listet opp innholdskravene til de to skjemaene.
selection_criteria: Søknaden blir vurdert av faglig utvalg for tverrfaglige ordninger . Utvalget leser og diskuterer alle søknadene og bruker sin samlede kompetanse til å bestemme hvilke prosjekter som skal få tilskudd. Søknadene vurderes enkeltvis og i sammenheng med de andre søknadene i samme søknadsrunde. Kulturrådet ønsker å fremme et mangfold av aktører, uttrykk og estetiske praksiser, aktivitet i hele landet og at barn og ungdom møter kunst og kultur. Disse målsettingene blir tatt med i totalvurderingen når utvalget skal fordele budsjettrammen de har til rådighet. Når utvalget vurderer hver enkelt søknad, legger de overordnet vekt på det kunstneriske/faglige innholdet kvalitetene i prosjektet i hvilken grad prosjektet er relevant for ordningens formål om prosjektet er gjennomførbart Utvalget ser særlig etter den faglige begrunnelsen for etableringen, oppgraderingene og/eller investeringene konkrete program-, formidlings- eller produksjonsplaner ved arenaen profesjonalitet og kunst- og kulturfaglig kompetanse og ledelse, nå og i framtiden et økonomisk grunnlag som viser at etableringen og/eller en langsiktig drift er gjennomførbar åpenhet i selskapsstruktur og økonomiflyt sosial bærekraft, tilgjengelighet, universell utforming og inkludering for alle publikumsgrupper lokal/regional forankring og stedsbevissthet hensiktsmessige, stedstilpassede og bærekraftige løsninger i arkitektur, materialbruk og teknikk klima- og naturhensyn i gjennomføringen, for eksempel gjennom ombruk, omstilling, gjenbruk, flerbruk og energieffektivisering av bygg, utstyr og infrastruktur om vilkår for tidligere tilskudd er fulgt opp, slik som krav til rapportering, regnskap og gjennomføring Søker du på vegne av en virksomhet med fast årlig statstilskudd, legger utvalget også vekt på om prosjektet bidrar til samarbeid med det frie feltet om prosjektet tilbyr infrastruktur som aktører i det frie feltet kan benytte om prosjektet utvider og/eller utvikler virksomhetens aktiviteter eller dekningsområde nivået på virksomhetens årlige statstilskudd virksomhetens egeninnsats/bidrag til prosjektet
project_requirements_en: The arena or infrastructure you are applying for funding for must be used for professional arts and cultural activity, or for collaboration between professional and voluntary arts and cultural life. The project you are applying for funding for must benefit the arts and culture fields and/or a general audience. The Arts Council assumes that the project is carried out in accordance with public law. We do not provide funding for developing arenas for private business activity and premises that are only to be rented out on commercial terms pure production or workshop premises that are only accessible to individual artists or a smaller group of artists/actors enterprises where public debt negotiations or bankruptcy proceedings have been opened ordinary operations to buy buildings or property to buy personal equipment, supplies, consumables or artworks to buy equipment for the purpose of (commercial) rental activities scenography or decoration kitchen and catering facilities measures that belong under other grant schemes in the Arts Council
how_to_apply_en: The application must be submitted through the Arts Council’s application portal. You can choose between two different form types: Investment support cultural buildings: for applications for grants to convert, upgrade or adapt existing premises and infrastructure, for new construction and to purchase technical equipment for presentation or production. Individual projects: for applications for grants for preliminary projects or pilot projects. Examples of this are needs analyses, feasibility studies, sketch projects or planning of buildings or measures, clarification of zoning regulations, architectural competitions or other measures that fall within the purpose of the scheme. Below we have listed the content requirements for the two forms.
selection_criteria_en: The application is assessed by the professional committee for interdisciplinary schemes . The committee reads and discusses all applications and uses its collective expertise to determine which projects will receive funding. The applications are assessed individually and in relation to the other applications in the same application round. The Arts Council wants to promote a diversity of actors, expressions and aesthetic practices, activity throughout the country and that children and young people encounter art and culture. These objectives are taken into account in the overall assessment when the committee is to allocate the budget framework available to them. When the committee assesses each individual application, it places overall emphasis on the artistic/professional content the qualities of the project the extent to which the project is relevant to the purpose of the scheme whether the project is feasible The committee particularly looks for the professional justification for the establishment, upgrades and/or investments concrete program, dissemination or production plans at the venue professionalism and arts and culture professional competence and management, now and in the future an economic basis showing that the establishment and/or long-term operation is feasible transparency in corporate structure and financial flows social sustainability, accessibility, universal design and inclusion for all audience groups local/regional anchoring and place awareness appropriate, site-adapted and sustainable solutions in architecture, material use and technology climate and nature considerations in implementation, for example through reuse, transition, recycling, multifunctional use and energy efficiency of buildings, equipment and infrastructure whether conditions for previous grants have been followed up, such as requirements for reporting, accounts and implementation If you are applying on behalf of an enterprise with fixed annual state funding, the committee also places emphasis on whether the project contributes to collaboration with the independent field whether the project offers infrastructure that actors in the independent field can use whether the project expands and/or develops the enterprise’s activities or area of coverage the level of the enterprise’s annual state funding the enterprise’s own contribution/contribution to the project

title: Different art forms
requirements_text:
The Danish Art Foundation’s committees welcome all applications that border on or go beyond traditional art forms.
Your application must obviously meet the general requirements for the funding programme that your application is directed to.
requirements_text_en:
The Danish Art Foundation’s committees welcome all applications that border on or go beyond traditional art forms.
Your application must obviously meet the general requirements for the funding programme that your application is directed to.
project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.
When you break down your project into several applications, it is important that you also split up your budget, since you are not able to get the same expenses covered by more than one funding programme.
Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.
In some cases, two or more committees join together to fund a grant.
This will often happen, if a project’s budget is too large for one committee to fund it all.

project_requirements:
The applicant will undertake a residency at CentroCentro Cibeles from 4th until the 31 st of May 2015, during which they will be required to run a series of workshops with primary school pupils from schools in the municipality of Madrid.

The description must include the following information:
1. The age range at which the project is aimed, bearing in mind that in Spain primary education covers from 6 to 12 years of age.
2. Project plan and timescales, with information such as number of sessions and how long they last (taking into account that the school day runs from 9am to 4pm).
3. Approximate budget and description of the material to be used, which will have to be approved by MADRID DESTINO

•If necessary, between 1 and 3 illustrations relating to the project that may consist of pictures or texts (which should no longer than 500 words each).

•Letter explaining the reasons why the applicant is applying for the residency.
